subject: Is there a way to plot a trees in same scale?

messages.author: 0636c591dc0d6576
messages.subject: Is there a way to plot a trees in same scale?
parts:
hi,

I am trying to plot multiple trees (using gridExtra) on the same scale in one figure. Is it possible to specify the xlim and ylim so that all trees are plotted on same scale? Also, once i plot the tree, I did not see an option in geom_treescale() to show the desired scale. Is that an option? or Does it always gets picked automatically?

Thank you for responding to multiple questions.

migun

messages.author: 2a4584b898b0bd00
messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to plot a trees in same scale?
parts:
> x=list(rtree(10), rtree(20), rtree(30))
> class(x) = "multiPhylo"
> ggtree(x) + facet_wrap(~.id, scales="fixed")

messages.author: 0636c591dc0d6576
messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to plot a trees in same scale?
parts:
I will give that a a a try.

But, here is a working example:

# tree 1
> raxml_file <- system.file("extdata/RAxML", "RAxML_bipartitionsBranchLabels.H3", package="ggtree")
> raxml <- read.raxml(raxml_file)
> p1<-ggtree(raxml) + geom_label(aes(label=bootstrap, fill=bootstrap)) + geom_tiplab() + geom_treescale()

#tree2
> nwk <- system.file("extdata", "sample.nwk", package="ggtree")
> p2 <- ggtree(read.tree(nwk)) %>% groupClade(node=21) + aes(color=group, linetype=group)  + geom_treescale()

I used multiplot to draw two panels together, but i couldn't find a parameter that controls the size of each plot so that they are both drawn on same scale. Both of these trees have different branch lengths (equivalent to scale), but wanted to draw on same scale to show the stark difference.
Thank you
